[THOUGHT] 
This is a patient with advanced, untreated HIV who developed subacute (days–weeks) right leg weakness and new somnolence/confusion. MRI brain shows disseminated, nonenhancing white-matter lesions without mass effect — a classic radiographic pattern for demyelinating opportunistic infection in immunosuppression. The clinical picture is subacute focal neurologic deficits plus cognitive change, which fits progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) due to JC virus. CSF JC PCR can be falsely negative; CSF otherwise unremarkable and there is no mass effect or ring enhancement to suggest toxoplasmosis or lymphoma. Other causes (toxoplasmosis, primary CNS lymphoma, bacterial abscess, ischemic stroke, MS, HIV encephalopathy) are less consistent with the imaging pattern and clinical subacute focal deficits. Therefore the single most likely diagnosis is PML from JC virus in the setting of severe untreated HIV; definitive diagnosis may require repeat CSF testing or brain biopsy if needed.

Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (JC virus) in the setting of advanced untreated HIV infection.
